definition: General Arabic word for 'opening' or 'orifice,' applied colloquially and crudely to the anus.
notes: Base meaning is any opening such as a volcano's mouth or gun muzzle; its use for the anus is contextual and crude rather than clinical.

definition: The uterus; the standard Modern Standard Arabic clinical term for the womb where a fetus develops.
notes: Homographic with رحم (raḥm, 'mercy') — a distinct Arabic word sharing the same consonantal root; context disambiguates.

definition: The ovary; the paired female gonad that produces ova and sex hormones.
notes: Literally 'egg-producer' from root ب-ي-ض; singular form, plural is مبايض (mabāyiḍ).

definition: The Fallopian tube; the paired duct connecting each ovary to the uterus, the usual site of fertilization.
notes: قناة = canal/duct; فالوب = phonetic rendering of the eponym Fallopius. Mapped to vas_deferens as the closest registry analogue (the male ductal equivalent).

definition: The cervix; literally 'neck of the womb,' the narrow lower portion of the uterus opening into the vaginal canal.
notes: Transparent anatomical calque: عنق = neck, رحم = womb. Standard in clinical and health-education Arabic.

definition: The female reproductive system; the complete set of organs involved in female reproduction, including ovaries, Fallopian tubes, uterus, and vagina.
notes: Registry concept 'genitalia' covers external organs only; this term encompasses the entire internal and external system. Match is approximate.

definition: An ovum; the female gamete (egg cell) produced by the ovary and capable of being fertilized by a sperm cell.
notes: Diminutive of بيضة (bayḍa, egg). Registry concept 'ovaries' is the closest match — that organ produces بويضات; the gamete cell itself has no dedicated registry slug.

definition: The uterus; the definite-article form of رحم, the standard MSA term for the womb used in clinical, religious, and everyday discourse.
notes: Functionally identical to entry رحم with the Arabic definite article al-; the definite form predominates in written MSA.

definition: The prostate gland; a phonetic loanword from English/Latin used in modern Arabic medical communication.
notes: Also rendered البروستات (al-brūstāt). Competes with the native descriptive phrase الغدة البروستاتية; both are used in clinical settings.

definition: The spermatic cord; the bundle of nerves, blood vessels, and vas deferens connecting each testis to the inguinal canal.
notes: Literally 'seminal cord.' Mapped to vas_deferens as closest registry entry; anatomically the spermatic cord contains the vas deferens as one of its several components.

definition: Seminiferous tubule or seminal duct; a context-dependent clinical term for either the sperm-producing tubules within the testis or the ductal transport system.
notes: Literally 'seminal tube/pipe.' Mapped to vas_deferens as closest registry entry; anatomically distinct — seminiferous tubules are the site of spermatogenesis inside the testes.

definition: The male reproductive system; the complete set of organs involved in male reproduction, encompassing testes, epididymides, vas deferens, prostate, seminal vesicles, and penis.
notes: Registry concept 'male_genitalia' covers external organs only; this term encompasses the entire internal and external reproductive apparatus. Match is approximate.

definition: The prostate gland; a formally descriptive clinical Arabic phrase specifying both the organ type (gland) and its identity.
notes: الغدة = gland; البروستاتية = adjectival loanword. More formally precise than البروستاتا; preferred in written medical and academic texts.

definition: The pubic area; the mons pubis and surrounding pubic region, the zone between the lower abdomen and the external genitalia.
notes: Standard clinical and religious-legal term; central to Islamic jurisprudence on awrah boundaries and hygiene; removal of pubic hair (istiḥdād) is a recommended sunnah practice.

definition: Pubic hair; the hair growing on and around the pubic mound and genitalia.
notes: شعر = hair; العانة = the pubic region. Extensively discussed in Islamic hygiene literature; removal is a recommended sunnah act in hadith tradition.

definition: The genital region; a clinical euphemism referring broadly to the anatomical area of the genitalia without specifying individual organs.
notes: Literally 'the reproductive zone.' Preferred in broadcast journalism and health campaigns as an inoffensive, non-specific anatomical reference.

definition: Sexual intercourse; the primary Classical and Modern Standard Arabic term for coitus, used across medical, religious, and legal discourse.
notes: From root ج-م-ع (to gather/join); the dominant term in Islamic jurisprudence (fiqh) and classical Arabic medicine; frank but not crude in MSA register.

definition: Sexual intercourse; a literary Arabic term literally meaning 'lying together,' used in classical literature and formal prose as a circumlocution for coitus.
notes: From ضجع (to lie down); more literary and euphemistic than جماع; found in classical Arabic literary texts and formal prose rather than everyday speech or legal writing.

definition: Sex; the most common modern colloquial MSA word for sexual activity, also serving as the standard word for 'gender,' 'type,' or 'species.'
notes: Polysemous: means 'kind/type,' 'gender,' and in modern usage 'sex (intercourse).' The sexual meaning is fully established in contemporary MSA; context disambiguates.

definition: Sexual intercourse; a Classical Arabic term implying penetration, used extensively in Islamic jurisprudence as the technical marker for legally consequential coitus.
notes: From وطأ (to tread upon/step on); mahr, iddah, and hadd punishments in fiqh hinge on whether وطء occurred; more vivid and legalistic than جماع.

definition: Sexual intercourse; a clinical compound phrase meaning 'direct sexual contact,' standard in health communication and legal language.
notes: مباشرة = direct contact/dealing; جنسية = sexual (adjectival). The standard euphemistic clinical phrase in broadcast media and public health Arabic.

definition: Penetration; the act of insertion of the penis into a bodily orifice, a Classical Arabic legal term central to Islamic jurisprudence on ritual purity and criminal law.
notes: From root و-ل-ج (to enter/insert); the technical legal trigger for hadd punishments (ḥadd al-zinā) in classical fiqh — many rulings hinge on whether إيلاج occurred. Romanization in source input (ījlāj) may contain a transposition; standard rendering is īlāj.

definition: Reproduction; the biological process of producing offspring through sexual union; used loosely in clinical contexts for sexual intercourse as the reproductive act.
notes: From نسل (offspring/progeny); primarily denotes biological reproduction rather than the sex act per se; mapped to intercourse_generic as copulation is the implied mechanism.

definition: Sexual intercourse; a euphemistic term literally meaning 'approach' or 'drawing near,' used as a delicate circumlocution for coitus in formal and religious prose.
notes: From قرب (to be near/approach); a softer alternative to جماع, preferred in health education materials and formal prose seeking to avoid blunt terminology.

definition: Sexual intercourse; a Classical Arabic term derived from 'falling upon,' with connotations of physical consummation and sometimes dominance.
notes: From وقع (to fall/occur upon); more vivid and crude-leaning than جماع; appears in classical Arabic erotica and some fiqh texts; less frequent in modern MSA than جماع or جنس.
